source.title: Geometry of Confabulation and Refusal in Small Language Models

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests the V4 implication that an SAE can recover sparse features in an LLM, using SAE analysis and interventions rather than the original toy-model superposition setup. It does not test superposition or capacity competition directly.
record.gate_note: The SAE results bear on V4's SAE-recoverability alternative. The paper does not test whether LLM features are superposed, whether features compete for dimensions, or whether neurons spread features across dimensions. The probe, refusal-direction, and correctness results are not rows for the superposition versions. Values used only to select SAE features or intervention settings are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study is about refusal versus confabulation. It uses an off-the-shelf Qwen-Scope SAE as a tool to decompose its refusal direction and to pick a steering handle. It does not ask whether LLM features are superposed, spread across neurons, or generally recoverable by SAEs, and it does not test SAE features as canonical units. Its SAE results describe the refusal mechanism rather than giving a rate or test of superposition. The reader's T2/V4 'supports' reading treats tool use as a test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record covers only the SAE subsection. The main conclusions are threefold. (i) A late-layer refusal-vs-confabulation signal beats prompt-feature baselines on Qwen3-1.7B and Gemma 2 2B, and a single direction causally controls the first-token refusal opener, though only about a third of Qwen's openings complete as refusals. (ii) The correctness-probe signal is model-dependent: large and portable for Llama 3.2 3B (+21–25 pp), near prompt-baseline level for Qwen, and attributed to post-training rather than scale. (iii) On Qwen, the SAE splits the refusal direction into register features, one of which (2191) is causally sufficient for the opener, and no concentrated confabulation feature is found.
record.recipe_differences: The original source concerns toy-model superposition; this paper probes and intervenes on LLM hidden states and SAE decoder features, without testing feature overlap or capacity competition.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE reconstruction quality depends on applying the base-trained SAE to the instruct model at its declared hook. The causal effect is dose-dependent; controls are reported at sub-norm doses, and a random direction shows a possible magnitude effect at a super-norm dose.

fits_no_version.finding: The Qwen-Scope SAE trained on Qwen3-1.7B-Base reconstructs Instruct-model post-block-27 residuals at per-item EV 0.50 (cosine 0.72) on 549 items. An earlier EV 0.82 figure came from the wrong hook.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs trained on a base model transfer only marginally to the instruct model at the same hook.

fits_no_version.finding: A probe-derived refusal direction decomposes into several correlated register features (4314, 17077, 14034, 2191). Only 2191's decoder direction causally writes the opener; the decoder directions of 14034 and 17077 produce no matching tokens when pushed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correlational SAE decomposition of a behaviour direction includes features that are not causally active for that behaviour.

record.problems: The SAE is trained on Qwen3-1.7B-Base but applied to the instruct model, with marginal reconstruction quality at the declared hook. The causal feature result uses 30 wrong items. The negative search covers one dictionary at one hook; the authors note feature splitting and absorption risks. No direct superposition, feature-overlap, neuron-spread, or canonical-unit test is performed.
record.rows_left_out: No additional version-relevant SAE outcome rows omitted.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transitions or feature geometry.
No test of capacity competition or of dedicated vs shared dimensions.
No analysis of the origins of polysemantic neurons.
SAE used only as a tool on one refusal direction. No measurement of features spreading across neurons, and no general test of SAE recoverability.
Splitting and absorption risk is mentioned but not tested. No completeness, stability or canonicality test.
Uses 1-D directions throughout, but never compares them with multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. The SAE serves as an instrument for studying refusal, and its results are scoped by the authors to one dictionary at one hook with EV 0.50. All rows are unlinked from V4, and the reader's V4 supports and limits_scope labels are dropped. Row r6 is a control for the steering method and should be removed.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, feature sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity arises from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.

The paper tests SAE recovery for refusal-related features in Qwen3-1.7B. It does not measure whether features spread across many neurons, or establish how general SAE recoverability is across features or LLMs.
The paper cautions that SAE features may split or absorb features, but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The paper studies directions and SAE decoder vectors, but does not test whether the underlying superposed features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B
rows.operation_detail: Measured SAE feature 2191 activation on refusal and wrong items.
rows.measure: Feature hit rate and mean activation
rows.value: Refusal-item hit rate: 100%; mean activation on refusals: 268
rows.note: The feature's decoder lens corresponds to refusal-opening vocabulary.
rows.check: Hit rate of one selected SAE feature on refusal vs wrong items characterises refusal, not whether LLMs contain sparse dictionary-recoverable features in general. The feature was chosen by the study's own ranking views, so this is close to a selection value.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B
rows.operation_detail: Added the unit-normalized decoder direction for SAE feature 2191 to the residual and measured whether the next-token argmax was a refusal opener.
rows.measure: Wrong-item next-token argmax in refusal-opener set
rows.note: The paper reports the feature saturates at a dose equal to 0.46× the mean state norm.
rows.check: This is a steering result (30/30 opener flips at α=750) for the refusal behaviour. It tests the causal role of a refusal feature, not superposition or SAE recoverability.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B
rows.operation_detail: Measured the SAE feature 4314 activation hit rate by label.
rows.note: The paper describes this as the strongest refusal-vs-wrong discriminator among the listed ensemble features.
rows.check: Hit rate of a feature chosen as the strongest discriminator (diff-z ranking): a selection statistic, not a superposition measure.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B
rows.operation_detail: Measured the SAE feature 17077 activation hit rate by label.
rows.note: The paper identifies it as a register marker; it does not report a causal test of this feature.
rows.check: Hit rate of a feature from the selection ranking; describes the refusal ensemble, not superposition.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B
rows.operation_detail: Searched the SAE dictionary for features marking wrong answers or confabulation.
rows.measure: Presence of a concentrated confabulation feature
rows.value: No concentrated dictionary feature or token signature for confabulation was found; the strongest wrong-side features were topic, phrasing, and attempt-formatting cues.
rows.note: The authors scope this negative finding to one dictionary at one hook and note that absence of a dictionary feature does not imply absence of signal.
rows.check: The failure to find a confabulation feature concerns the confabulation mechanism. The authors say absence of a dictionary feature is not absence of signal, so it cannot bear on V4.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B
rows.operation_detail: Applied three norm-matched random directions and a shuffled-label probe direction using the intervention protocol.
rows.measure: Refusal and refusal-opener rates under control directions
rows.baseline: Real directions at α=-500: 6–12/30 refusals remained refusing; at α=+500 to +1500: 27–30% judged refusals and 97–100% opener rates on wrong items.
rows.value: Controls at α=-500: 29–30/30 refusals remained refusing; at α=+500 to +1500: ≤13% judged refusals and ≤40% opener rates on wrong items.
rows.note: One random seed partially collapsed refusals at the super-norm dose α=-2000; the reported working regime is at or below the state norm.
rows.check: This is a control for the study's own steering method (random and shuffled directions), not a result on any version. It should not be a row.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B
rows.operation_detail: Checked reconstruction by the Qwen-Scope SAE trained on the base model, applied to the instruct model at the SAE's declared hook.

conditions.value: Qwen3-1.7B-Base SAE applied to Qwen3-1.7B Instruct

rows.measure: Per-item explained variance and mean cosine reconstruction quality
rows.note: The authors characterize base-to-instruct transfer reconstruction quality as marginal; an earlier EV=0.82/cosine=0.90 check used a different hook and did not measure the SAE at its declared contract.
rows.check: A tool-fit check of a base-trained SAE applied to the instruct model (EV 0.50, cosine 0.72). It is a reconstruction diagnostic for this transfer, not a test of whether the model's features are sparse or superposed. Recorded under fits_no_version.

relation.reason: SAE decomposition supplies descriptive coordinates and a causal steering handle, without testing feature overlap, capacity competition, or dictionary completeness, stability, or canonicality.

tranche.reason: Uses an existing SAE to analyze and steer refusal. The reconstruction check diagnoses base-to-instruct tool transfer; it does not test a superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: Appendix D.2 confirms EV 0.50 (median 0.51) and cosine 0.72 over 549 items at the declared hook. Earlier EV 0.82/cosine 0.90 used the post-block-23 residual.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The SAE recovers refusal-register features, including feature 2191, whose decoder direction flips 30/30 wrong-item next-token argmaxes to refusal openers (r1–r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Qwen3-1.7B confabulation-related SAE features and base-to-instruct reconstruction
reader_labels.reason: The search finds no concentrated confabulation feature, and reconstruction quality for the base-trained SAE on the instruct model is described as marginal (r5, r7).
